findings.stat_label: Fewer U.S. apartment completions through Q3 2026 than in the same period of 2025
findings.period: January to September 2026 vs. same period 2025
findings.headline: Supply is slowing nationally. Phoenix is still delivering.
findings.signal: About 231,000 units were completed nationally through Q3, down 27% from a year earlier. Q3 delivered a little over 82,000 units. That was up for a second straight quarter, but still the smallest third quarter since 2019 and the fifth straight quarter under 100,000.
findings.source: RealPage Analytics, U.S. Apartment Supply Update 3rd Quarter 2026

local.evidence: Phoenix was among the five metros RealPage named for the most new deliveries in Q3 2026, each above 3,000 units, alongside Dallas, Houston, Austin and Atlanta.
local.limitation: No verified public figure on Phoenix rents, occupancy or concessions was available this week.

decision.question: Are your concessions priced for the competition you face today, or for the pressure of six months ago?
decision.examine: Before changing concessions, compare nearby lease ups still delivering, the effective rent trend, renewal conversion and recent concession changes at comps. A national slowdown alone does not justify cutting concessions in a market still delivering at volume.

watch.owner: LocalLift research desk; graded in the Signal Ledger

findings.interpretation: National supply relief is real, but Phoenix is likely to feel it later than the national figure suggests because it was still among the highest delivery metros in Q3.
findings.confidence: Medium (one quarter of completion counts; no verified local rent, occupancy or concession data).

monthly.headline: New supply is far below its peak. Rents have barely moved, and Phoenix is still delivering.
monthly.summary: Deliveries are well below their 2024 peak and the national vacancy index has eased from its February high. Asking rents range from slightly down to slightly up depending on the source, and rent inflation trails overall inflation. Locally, Phoenix remained one of the busiest delivery markets in Q3, so national relief should not be read as local relief.

monthly.method: Figures come from each publisher's own public release and are checked against it before publication. Licensed data is cited at the level the publisher made public, never reproduced. Rent measures differ by source, so figures are compared within a source. The Local Reality, Operator Decision and interpretation lines are ours. Every interpretation is logged in the Signal Ledger with a confidence level and graded at its checkpoint.
